workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.meaning: The governed project context that owns configuration, state, work, and policy.
workspace.sourceOfTruth: one workspace record resolved from the project root

workspace-preset.label: Workspace Preset
workspace-preset.meaning: A reusable workspace-wide selection of intake taxonomy, artifact defaults, tone, skills, and procedures.

source.label: Source
source.meaning: An external or internal signal origin connected to a Workspace through a cursor-based ingestion contract.
source.sourceOfTruth: source records scoped to a Workspace

objective.label: Objective
objective.meaning: A durable desired result and its rationale, advanced by one or more Work records.
objective.sourceOfTruth: objective records scoped to a Workspace

directive.label: Directive
directive.meaning: A standing instruction that generates Objectives or Work until retired.
directive.sourceOfTruth: directive records scoped to a Workspace

work.label: Work
work.meaning: One bounded, owned unit that advances an Objective and is projected to an external tracker when needed.
work.sourceOfTruth: Construct Work record; external trackers are projections

work-specification.label: Work Specification
work-specification.meaning: The versioned what-and-why agreement for one Work record.
work-specification.sourceOfTruth: immutable Work Specification versions owned by Work

plan.label: Plan
plan.meaning: A versioned approach that decomposes one Work Specification into Assignments.
plan.sourceOfTruth: immutable Plan versions owned by Work

run.label: Run
run.meaning: One execution attempt of a Plan, including checkpoints, Assignment state, approvals, and usage.
run.sourceOfTruth: Run records scoped to a Workspace and Plan

worker-profile.label: Worker Profile
worker-profile.meaning: An assignable worker configuration: runtime, model tier, skill emphasis, procedure affinity, and policy fence.

skill.label: Skill
skill.meaning: Reusable domain knowledge or operating guidance loaded by a worker.

procedure.label: Procedure
procedure.meaning: A reusable, named, deterministic sequence that Plans invoke.

assignment.label: Assignment
assignment.meaning: A bounded execution unit from a Plan, owned by one worker and governed by an explicit contract.
assignment.sourceOfTruth: assignment records owned by the active Plan and Run

capability.label: Capability
capability.meaning: A typed operation the system can perform, with inputs, outputs, preconditions, and postconditions.

policy.label: Policy
policy.meaning: A rule governing authority, approval, and external effects at the mutation boundary.

artifact.label: Artifact
artifact.meaning: A content-identified output produced by a Run or Assignment.
artifact.sourceOfTruth: Artifact record plus content hash and immutable output location

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.meaning: A typed assertion that an Artifact satisfies a requirement; represented as a relationship, not a standalone domain record.
evidence.sourceOfTruth: evidenced-by graph edge with requirement, verdict, provenance, and acceptance metadata

projection.label: Projection
projection.meaning: A derived adapter view of Construct-owned state, such as an external tracker item.
projection.sourceOfTruth: the Construct domain record being projected

graph-node.label: Graph Node
graph-node.meaning: A non-authoritative graph representation of a domain object or implementation entity.
graph-node.sourceOfTruth: the represented domain store or checked-in implementation file

graph-edge.label: Graph Edge
graph-edge.meaning: A typed, provenance-bearing relationship between Graph Nodes.
graph-edge.sourceOfTruth: declared or derived relationship with provenance and confidence

team: ordinary group of people in prose
workflow: generic human work process when no Construct object is named
contract: an executable input/output or provider boundary
a legal agreement in ordinary prose
org: an external organization in ordinary prose
deprecated: a third-party API lifecycle state when factually required
legacy: a third-party or historical file format when factually required

historicalExclusions.rule: Retired identifiers may appear only as evidence of a past decision or observed implementation. They must not be stated as current guidance, copied into examples, or emitted by generators.

currentToCanonical.lib/roles/: lib/worker-profiles/ or lib/policy/ according to responsibility

obsoleteSurfaces.retirementPolicy: These names may appear only in docs/obsolete/ historical evidence and never in active code, package payloads, generated adapters, or fixtures.
